_comment: Project-scoped Claude Code config. Loaded by cloud apps (iOS, Mac, web) that can't reach the user's ~/.claude/. Each project hook script begins with a self-skip preamble: if ~/.claude/hooks/<basename> exists (local CLI), the project copy exits 0 and the user-level master fires. On cloud sandboxes ~/.claude/hooks/ does not exist, so the project copy runs. See .claude/CLOUD.md.
_comment_permissions: Server-level MCP allow: 'mcp__<server>' pre-approves the Claude_Code_Remote tools that are NOT marked requiresUserInteraction (get_session, list_triggers, delete_trigger, ...). Cloud sessions name the server 'Claude_Code_Remote' (tools are mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__*), so the old 'claude-code-remote' entry never matched and add_repo/send_later kept hitting the approval wall (BRO-4216); both spellings are listed. Harmless on local CLI where the server isn't connected. KNOWN LIMIT (BRO-4236): add_repo, send_later and create_trigger are marked requiresUserInteraction, which per code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ('Actions no mode auto-approves') prompts even when an allow rule matches, in every mode. No allow rule or mode fixes that; don't re-add rules for them. Instead the PreToolUse hook block-prompting-remote-tools.sh denies the calls that have a prompt-free equivalent before the prompt appears.

hooks.command: G="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; R="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$G}"; H="$R/.claude/hooks/worktree-enforce.sh"; if [ -n "$R" ] && [ -f "$H" ]; then exec bash "$H"; elif [ -n "$R" ]; then printf '{"systemMessage":"Hook script missing, skipped (fail-open, BRO-4238): %s"}\n' "$H"; exit 0; else echo "FATAL: cannot resolve hook script $H (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-unset}, PWD=$PWD, git-toplevel=${G:-none})" >&2; exit 2; fi
